title: DFS in Alfama: Find the Route Deep First! 🚶‍♂️
description: Watch Depth-First Search (DFS) explore Alfama’s street graph by going as deep as possible before backtracking. The visualization shows how traversal order and visited-state control shape the path you find.
ig_caption:
🧭✨ DFS in the winding lanes of Alfama!

Depth-First Search (DFS) tackles a street-map graph by diving down one path at a time (LIFO/recursion or an explicit stack), then backtracking when it hits a dead end. 🧠🔁 In graph theory terms, DFS systematically traverses vertices (intersections) and edges (roads), using a **visited set** to prevent cycles—crucial on real maps with loops and one-ways.

📍Here’s the twist: because DFS is not inherently shortest-path, the “found” route depends on neighbor ordering—exactly like choices between adjacent streets in Alfama’s grid-like-but-not-quite layout. 🏘️🗺️

✅ Want to see DFS vs BFS or A* on the same map? Comment your favorite algorithm and I’ll generate the next visualization!

🎥 Follow for more real-map pathfinding + coding reels!
